description: Program-check rules. Effective sets use the same fractional counting as the volume panel (rating >= 0.25). Severity: warn = worth fixing, info = judgment call. v7: adds rule pattern_gap (movement slots from patterns.json) and fix action add_slot_exercise.

rules.message: {day} has {n} exercises averaging under 2 sets each. That's a lot of setup for little work. Merge some into fewer exercises with 3 sets.
{day} has {sets} hard sets, above the {max} cap for your level. Move some sets to another day.
rules.message_info: {day} has {sets} hard sets, close to the {max} cap for your level.

rules.message: {day} runs about {min} minutes. Past 90, focus and output drop. Cut sets or split the day.
rules.message_info: {day} runs about {min} minutes. That's long, so make sure the big lifts come first.

rules.message: {day} has {sets} heavy squat and deadlift sets, above {max}. Move some to another day or swap in a machine variant.
rules.message_week: {sets} heavy squat and deadlift sets this week, above {max}. Swap some for machine or supported variants.

rules.message: {muscle} gets {sets} effective sets on {day}. Past about 10 in one session, extra sets mostly add fatigue. Move some to another day.
{exercise} on {day} has {sets} sets. More than 5 sets of one exercise gives diminishing returns. Use 2 to 4 sets, or split it across two exercises.
{muscle} is trained meaningfully on only {n} day this week. Splitting its sets over 2 or more days makes higher volume easier to do well; total weekly sets matter most.
rules.message_indirect_only: Only indirect work so far. Add a direct exercise for {muscle}.
rules.message_note: Use message_indirect_only when the muscle has weekly sets > 0 but no single day reaches min_effective_to_count; otherwise use message.
rules.message_evidence: Volume-matched studies find little growth difference by frequency (Schoenfeld 2019, Pelland 2026); see education/fundamentals/volume-frequency.json.

rules.message: The {pattern} exercises on {day} add up to {sets} effective sets for {muscle}, past about 10 in one session. Cut sets or move one to another day.
rules.note: Any number of exercises from the same pattern is fine. This only fires when the pattern's exercises together push one muscle over the per-session cap.

rules.message: Pull-to-push sets are {ratio}:1 this week. A common programming guideline keeps pulling between about 75% of pushing and 2x pushing, so the upper body is trained evenly. The band is a coaching convention, not a tested threshold.
rules.message_no_pull: No pulling yet. Add a row or pulldown to balance your pressing.
rules.message_no_push: No pushing yet. Add a press to balance your pulling.
rules.ratio_note: ratio = pull_sets / push_sets. If push_sets = 0 and pull_sets > 0, the checker emits ratio 99 and the app shows message_no_push. If pull_sets = 0 and push_sets > 0, the ratio is 0 and the app shows message_no_pull. If both are 0, no flag.

rules.message: No stretch-biased exercise for {muscle} this week. Add one, like {examples}. Training at long muscle lengths tends to build more muscle.
rules.severity_note: r2fix: warn for check_muscles (rules.stretch_check.checked), info for the others.

rules.message: A heavy deadlift on {day1} is followed by heavy squats on {day2}. The lower back and hips won't have recovered. Put at least a day between them.
rules.severity_note: Round 2: demoted from warn to info. The evidence is thin (Belcher 2019 found recovery after deadlifts no slower than after squats or bench press); shown as a note in Lower-back fatigue between days.

rules.message: {muscle} gets a solid session on both {day1} and {day2}. Give a muscle at least 48 hours between hard sessions.
{day} has both heavy squats and heavy deadlifts. For a beginner, that's too much lower-back fatigue in one day. Split them onto different days.
rules.severity_note: Round 2: demoted from warn to info. The evidence is thin (Belcher 2019 found recovery after deadlifts no slower than after squats or bench press); shown as a note in Lower-back fatigue between days.

rules.message: {muscle} is at {sets} weekly sets, outside the {min} to {max} target.
This week's recovery cost is {pct}% of your saved normal week. Expect more fatigue than usual.
rules.note: Compared to saved baseline week. Info above 115%, warn above 130%.

rules.severity_rule: warn when a slot in patterns.json `required` has 0 exercises this week; info when any slot is above 0 but below patterns.json weekly_min_by_level[level] (incl. a required slot at 1 of 2), or when a non-required slot with a min is at 0. Skipped on an empty board.
rules.counting: Each tile counts 1 for every slot its exercise lists. Compound slots count only primary/accessory exercises. counts_toward adds the count to those slots too (lunge -> squat).
rules.message: No {slot_lower} this week. Add one {slot_lower} exercise ({examples}).
rules.message_info: {slot_name}: {n} of {min} exercises this week for your level.
rules.message_note: {slot_lower} = slot name lowercased, e.g. 'No vertical pull this week.' {examples} = names of the top 2 slot_recommendations.

params.by: default 1; the checker tries 1, 2, ... up to the amount needed

reduce_sets.note: With lowest_priority_isolation, the checker can trim several isolation tiles in one fix, working from the last tile up, to bring a session under its cap. Each tile stays at 2 sets or more.

params.target: tile id; default the smallest isolation tile, then the smallest tile

move_tile.best_valid_day: Use only existing training days, never adding one. Rank days by (1) fewest neighbouring days where the tile's primary muscle is already at solid or above, (2) least load on that muscle, (3) fewest total sets. Take the first day whose result passes validation.

swap_exercise.note: lower_spinal means the candidate is not in heavy_squats or heavy_hinges and rates lower_back lower than the current exercise.

params.choose: Candidates are exercises in `staples` (every exercise used in any preset) that rate the muscle >= 0.75 and have type isolation or accessory. Leave out pattern plyometric, and leave out equipment rings, suspension, medicine ball and stability ball unless the board already uses that equipment. Use the full library only if no staple qualifies. Rank by swap.json score against the board's biggest contributor to the muscle, plus 20 x the candidate's rating. If nothing on the board trains the muscle, rank by 100 x rating - 10 x fatigue. For push_pull_imbalance when the board has no pulling, pick a horizontal_row or vertical_pull staple first. Break ties (scores within 0.05) by how many preset tiles use the exercise, most first, then by id.
params.to_day: lightest eligible day (fewest total sets) that doesn't already have the exercise

params.target: Tiles rating the muscle >= 0.5, highest rating first

reorder_day.preview: Reorder {day_name}: primaries, then accessories, then isolation

params.target: the tile with the most sets in the pattern
params.to: the best swap.json same-pattern alternative not already on that day, on the same day

split_pattern.preview: Split {name} on {day_name}: {from}→{keep} sets, plus {moved} sets of {new_name}

params.sets: n; both the source and any new tile keep at least 2 sets, and a tile already on the target day can't go past 5

params.into: a same-pattern tile on the same day, total no more than 5 sets

fix_actions._note: Previews use {day_name}, {to_day_name} and {from_day_name}, looked up in day_names. The raw keys {day}, {to_day} and {from_day} stay in params.
fix_actions.custom_exercises: Custom exercises are never fix candidates. No fix suggests, adds or swaps in a custom exercise. They can still appear as manual swap suggestions (see swap.json custom).

params.choose: patterns.slot_recommendations(slot, level, board) order (eligible only: not custom, can count for the slot), first 6 tried
params.to_day: days ordered by: has a tile in the same slot group (patterns.json slots[].group) first, then fewest total sets, then day order; skip a day that already has the exercise
params.sets: rules.pattern_gap_fix.sets_by_kind (compound 3, isolation 2); if that adds a flag, the same exercise/day is tried at 2 sets

fix_validation: Every fix candidate has to pass validation before it's shown. Apply it to a copy of the board and run every rule again. Drop the candidate if it creates any non-info flag that wasn't there before, including a new red weekly_volume. Drop it too if it doesn't move the targeted flag toward compliance (fewer sets, fewer minutes, a ratio or volume closer to range, or more training days for the muscle). A candidate that clears the flag is marked resolves=true. One that only improves it is marked resolves=false and shown after the ones that clear it. Try each rule's fixes in the order listed, prefer a resolving candidate within each action, keep one per action, and show at most 3. If none are valid, show none, and never show an unvalidated fix.
partial_label: Helps, but won't fully clear this

suggestions._note: v22 quick-apply: every suggestion the app shows gets preview + Apply + Undo using the v18 mechanism (validate on a board copy, fix_validation). Program-check sources reuse rules[].fixes. Analytics sources define their own trigger, candidates and metric here. Reference: tools/suggest.py suggest(days, level, baseline). Custom exercises are never candidates. Show at most 3 fixes per suggestion.
suggestions.validation: Apply to a copy of the board, run every program-check rule again, drop the candidate if it adds any non-info flag (incl. a new red weekly_volume), and drop it unless the success metric moves toward the goal. resolves=true when the goal is met; resolves=true first, partial ones get partial_label.

many_small_entries.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)

session_hard_sets.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)

session_length.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)
session_length.extra: Day header '~N min' is display only; fixes come from the session_length rule.

spinal_load.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)

junk_volume_session.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)
junk_volume_session.extra: Analytics curve's half-value discount past 10 sets is the same condition.

sets_per_exercise.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)

low_frequency.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)

redundant_pattern.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)

missing_stretch.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)

hinge_before_squat.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)

consecutive_high_volume.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)

beginner_squat_and_deadlift.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)

weekly_volume.success_metric: fix_validation (flag clears = resolves, else distance to compliance shrinks)

lower_fatigue_swap.trigger: each distinct exercise on the board that has at least one candidate
lower_fatigue_swap.scope: every tile of that exercise, on every day, except a day that already has the candidate
lower_fatigue_swap.candidate_rule: main muscle m = cur's highest rating. Candidate: not custom; same rules.json pattern as cur (cosine >= 0.6 if cur has no pattern); never compound->isolation; rating[m] >= cur rating[m] - 0.1; rating[m]/fatigue strictly higher. Order: rating/fatigue desc, swap.json score desc, id. Take the first that validates (try up to 8).
lower_fatigue_swap.preview: Swap {name} for {new_name} on {day_list} ({muscle}: {spf_from}→{spf_to} stimulus per fatigue)
lower_fatigue_swap.success_metric: week recovery cost (sum sets x fatigue) strictly lower; always resolves=true when valid

stretch_share.trigger: muscle in rules.stretch_biased with effective sets > 0 and share < stretch_share_flag_below (0.25)
stretch_share.candidate_rule: swap: board tiles rating m >= 0.5 that aren't stretch-biased for m, biggest sets x rating first (ties: day order, tile order); candidates from swap.json order that are in stretch_biased[m], same pattern or cosine >= 0.6, not custom, not already on that day; prefer the first that reaches 0.25. add: fix_actions.add_exercise with stretch=true (staples pool, 2 sets, lightest day).
stretch_share.success_metric: stretch share for m rises; resolves when >= 0.25

effective_frequency.where: analytics.js 'Frequency' dot rows (display) + check.js low_frequency note; same trigger as rule low_frequency
effective_frequency.trigger: muscle in frequency_muscles with fewer than 2 days at >= analytics.frequency_min_effective effective sets, and >= 2 training days
effective_frequency.candidate_rule: source day = day with most load on m. Tiles there rating m >= 0.5, biggest sets x rating first; move k = 2.. sets (source keeps >= 2, existing tile <= 5). Target days = training days under the frequency threshold for m, ranked (1) not next to a day already at threshold for m, (2) least load on m, (3) fewest total sets, (4) week order. add_exercise: fix_actions.add_exercise excluding the source day.
effective_frequency.success_metric: number of days at threshold for m rises; resolves at 2
effective_frequency.note: This replaces the low_frequency rule's own fix list in the UI so the two never disagree.

recovery_vs_baseline.where: check.js (app_only rule recovery_vs_baseline) + analytics.js 'Recovery cost' week %
recovery_vs_baseline.trigger: saved baseline exists and week cost x modifiers / baseline > info_above (1.15)
recovery_vs_baseline.candidate_rule: reduce: greedy, one set at a time from the tile with highest sets x fatigue (ties: higher fatigue, day order, tile order), each tile stays >= 2 sets, skip a step that would add a non-info flag, stop at <= 1.15. swap: exercises by fatigue desc then total sets, each swapped (all its tiles) to its first valid lower_fatigue_swap candidate, stop at <= 1.15. One combined fix each.
recovery_vs_baseline.success_metric: week cost % of baseline falls; resolves at <= 115%

weekly_band.where: heat.js body map week colours + analytics curve marker (blue = under min, amber = over max); red is rule weekly_volume
weekly_band.trigger: muscle week effective sets outside [level min (rounded to 0.5, >= 0.5), max] but not red
weekly_band.success_metric: effective weekly sets closer to range; resolves when inside
weekly_band.note: Optional: today the app colours these but shows no text. Show the quick fix in the muscle pop-up only.

pattern_gap.success_metric: slot count reaches the weekly min (flag clears = resolves; warn->info counts as resolving the warn); else count rises = partial

analysis_sheet.note: Analysis-sheet suggestions. Each type names its source (a key of this suggestions block, or a rules[] id whose fixes are used), the trigger and the edit. Candidates come from tools/suggest.py suggest(days, level, baseline) and are validated with suggestions.validation. Deterministic: same board, level and baseline -> same list.
analysis_sheet.apply: Apply = replace the board days with fix.days and keep the pre-apply board as the Undo snapshot (same as the old fixes.js applyFix). fix.diff is the same change as ops, for the preview, storage and history; tools/analysis.py apply_ops(days, diff) rebuilds the same tiles per day (appended tiles go last).
analysis_sheet.undo: Undo = restore the snapshot (equivalently, the inverse ops in reverse order). One level of Undo per applied suggestion; a later manual edit clears it.

edit_ops.sets: {op, day, id, from, to}: set that tile's sets to `to`. Undo: back to `from`.
edit_ops.swap: {op, day, from_id, to_id, sets}: replace the tile with from_id by to_id at the same position, same sets. Undo: swap back.
edit_ops.add: {op, day, id, sets}: append a tile at the end of the day. Undo: remove that appended tile.
edit_ops.remove: {op, day, id, sets}: remove the tile. Undo: re-insert it at its old position (kept in the Undo snapshot).

analysis_sheet.order: warn-sourced suggestions first (program-check warnings in checker order), then the types below in list order; within a type by target (muscle in targets.json order, day in week order).

types.label: Add sets to an under-target muscle
types.trigger: weekly effective sets < level min (weekly_band target.side under, not red; weekly_volume flag below the band: red)
edits: sets (+1 up to 5 on the highest-rated tile, fix_actions.add_sets)
types.success: sets closer to the range; resolves when inside

types.label: Trim sets from an over-target muscle
edits: sets (-1 at a time on the highest contributor, min 2; fix_actions.reduce_sets)

types.label: Spread a muscle over two days
types.trigger: effective_frequency or the low_frequency rule: muscle in frequency_muscles on fewer than 2 days at >= 2 effective sets, with >= 2 training days
types.success: days at threshold rises; resolves at 2

types.label: Swap in a stretch-biased exercise
types.trigger: stretch-biased share < 0.25 (stretch_share) or none at all (missing_stretch)

types.label: Swap for a lower-fatigue option
types.trigger: an exercise on the board has a same-pattern candidate with higher stimulus per fatigue

types.label: Bring recovery cost back to normal
types.trigger: saved baseline and week cost > 115% of it

types.label: Add a missing movement pattern
types.trigger: rules pattern_gap (warn: required slot at 0; info: below the level minimum)

types.label: Shorten a long or crowded day
types.trigger: session_length >= 90 min or hard sets above the level cap

types.label: Reduce heavy spine sets
types.trigger: heavy squat + hinge sets above the session or week cap

analysis_sheet.section_note: Round 2: every type has section (the Analysis section that shows it). program_check resolves per source through section_by_source; tools/analysis.py sheet() writes the resolved section on every entry.

logger.note: Logger coaching defaults (single source). User settings override per exercise.

prs.weight: Heaviest load completed for at least 1 rep in a working set.
prs.set_volume: Highest load x reps in a single working set.
prs.e1rm: Highest e1RM from a working set, using e1rm_formula, only sets with reps <= e1rm_max_reps.
prs.reps_at_load: Most reps in a working set at a load equal to or heavier than the load of the previous best for that many reps; shown as "rep PR". Also the only PR type for bodyweight sets with no added load.
prs.compare: strictly greater than every earlier logged working set of the same exercise id (aliases resolved), compared in kg internally
exclude: the first ever logged session of an exercise (sets the baseline, no badge)

tie.rule: Weight PR needs load > best + step_fraction x smallest real step (gap at that load in the saved active gym profile; no saved profile = logger.gym_profile_default[session unit], the same default gym suggestions use; equipment not described there = load_step[session unit][equipment]). set_volume and e1rm PRs need > best x (1 + review.flat_pct/100). reps_at_load treats earlier sets within step_fraction x step as the same load. Anything else is a tie: no badge. Removes kg/lb rounding PRs.
tie.why_weight_uses_step_not_pct: Loads are discrete; a real plate or dumbbell jump is a real weight PR even when under 1% (e.g. +2.5 lb microplates on a 300 lb lift). Conversion noise is always well under half a step.

suspect_decimal.note: v28.1 one-time cleanup for the keypad decimal bug (v24..v28B: a typed "." was dropped, 101.5 saved as 1015). Same rule as tools/prs.py suspect_decimal_sets: a done, loaded working set in a completed session started before saved_before is flagged when load_kg >= min_ratio x median(other loaded working sets of that exercise, kg) and |load_kg/divisor - median| <= window x median. Fewer than min_others other sets -> listed for a manual check (no fix). Fix = logged load / divisor.

completed_analytics.hard_sets: Working sets with at least 1 rep and RIR <= hardRIR or no RIR entered, credited to muscles with the same fractional weights as planning.
completed_analytics.volume: Sum of load x reps over working sets (warmups excluded), per session, per week and per muscle (weighted).
completed_analytics.load_trend: Per exercise, best e1RM per session over time.
completed_analytics.adherence: Completed planned working sets / planned working sets for sessions started in the week; also sessions done / sessions planned.
completed_analytics.note: These are logged totals, not estimates of muscle growth.

logger.jump_prefer_reps_above_note: v8 key kept for older builds; v29 uses load_jump (per type, gym profile aware).

load_jump.note: Double progression with real loads (tools/loads.py suggest_next). When every working set of the last session reached the top of the rep range at or below target RIR (missing RIR counts as meeting it), look up the next real load from the gym profile. If (next - current) / current x 100 <= max_jump_pct_by_type[type], suggest the next load with reps reset to the bottom of the range. Otherwise keep the load and suggest +1 rep (min reps of the top-load sets + 1), up to range top + rep_overshoot; once that cap is reached take the jump anyway (reps to range bottom). current = heaviest working load (assisted: least assistance); bodyweight exercises use effective load (logger.bodyweight). No heavier load in the gym: add reps to the cap, then action "max" (pick a harder variation). [M]

gym_profile_schema.note: One profile per gym, stored in settings (gymProfiles[], activeGymId). All weights in the profile unit. Anything not described falls back to load_step[unit][equipment] (a grid of multiples). Read by suggestions, the keypad/weight picker, plate calculator and warm-up rounding.

fields.name: string
fields.dumbbells: number[] per-hand weights that exist (logged load = one dumbbell)
fields.plates: [{weight, pairs}] plate pairs available for bars and plate-loaded machines
fields.microplates: [{weight, pairs}] fractional plates (optional), used like plates
fields.bars: {equipment: weight}, keys 'barbell','trap bar','smith machine','landmine','plate-loaded machine' (0 = log plates only)
fields.bar_by_exercise: {exercise_id: bar/sled weight} overrides (EZ bar, safety squat bar, a specific sled)
fields.stacks: {exercise_id | 'machine' | 'cable': {start, step, count} or {weights:[...]}, add_ons?: number[] (magnet/add-on weights, each usable once)}; exercise id beats equipment default

loads.barbell/trap bar/smith/plate-loaded: bar (or override) + 2 x any per-side combination of plates+microplates within the pair counts
loads.landmine: bar + any combination of single plates on one sleeve (each pair = 2 plates)
loads.machine/cable: stack weights + any subset of add_ons

gym_profile_schema.plate_calculator: plate_breakdown(load): fewest plates per side; if load cannot be built, the next lower achievable load with exact=false.

gym_profile_default.note: Used until Mr Dude edits his own profile; reproduces the v8 load_step grid for machines/cables. Edit to match the real gym.

bodyweight.note: Bodyweight-aware loads (#2). tools/prs.py flatten/detect_prs/completed_analytics. A model of the load moved, not a measurement.
bodyweight.log: history.bodyweights = [{date:'YYYY-MM-DD' (local), value, unit:'lb'|'kg'}]; manual, dated; any unit (converted with lbPerKg).
bodyweight.fraction_key: exercises.json bodyweight_fraction (0-1; omitted = external load only); bodyweight_basis = measured | derived | modeling.
bodyweight.effective_load: bodyweight_fraction x bodyweight + added load; exercises with bodyweight_assisted (assisted pull-up/dip machines): max(0, bodyweight_fraction x bodyweight - assistance). Logged load stays the added load (or the assistance); effective load is computed, never stored.
bodyweight.bodyweight_for_session: most recent entry dated on/before the session local date (startedAt||date); if every entry is later, the earliest entry is used and the set is marked backfilled (so logging bodyweight for the first time does not turn every later session into a PR).
not_effective: plate calculator / gym profile (added load only)
bodyweight.volume_split: completed_analytics.volume reports bodyweight_part_kg and external_kg alongside the totals.
bodyweight.no_bodyweight_logged: history has no bodyweights: fall back to added load only (v8 behaviour; a bodyweight set with no added load is reps-only, rep PRs only) and count the sets in completed_analytics.bodyweight.sets_without_bodyweight so the app can show a quiet "log your bodyweight" hint. Assisted machines without a bodyweight are reps-only (assistance is never treated as load).
bodyweight.recompute: Adding, editing or deleting a bodyweight entry recomputes PRs and analytics (same pure functions as recompute_on_edit). Expect a one-time badge reshuffle on bodyweight exercises the first time bodyweight is logged.
bodyweight.caveat: A bodyweight change moves the effective load, so a heavier Mr Dude can set a weight/e1RM PR on pull-ups at the same added load. That is by design (more mass moved) and labelled as estimated.

set_tags.note: Set-type tags (#3): set.tag = null | failure | myo_rep | drop_set | partials (one tag per set, one tap). Warm-ups are kind=warmup, not a tag. Credits and PR rules are modeling choices [M] informed by the cited studies; see data/v29-coach-spec.md.

failure.label: Failure
failure.why: A set to momentary failure is one hard set, no bonus: proximity-to-failure meta-regressions (Robinson 2024, Refalo 2023) show at most a small extra hypertrophy effect close to failure, so we do not weight it above an RIR 0-3 set.

myo_rep.label: Myo-rep match
myo_rep.logging: one row per myo-rep match set: load = activation load, reps = total reps across its mini-sets (optional mini_sets count). The activation set is its own untagged/failure row.
myo_rep.why: Rest-pause gave similar strength and similar or better hypertrophy than traditional sets in trained people (Prestes 2019, small n). Counted as 1 hard set (conservative). Total reps across mini-sets are not comparable with a straight set, so only the weight PR can come from it.

drop_set.label: Drop set
drop_set.logging: each drop is its own row tagged drop_set, right after the top set (untagged or failure). The top set counts as normal.
drop_set.why: Drop sets matched traditional sets for hypertrophy in the meta-analysis of Sødal 2023 (6 studies, mostly volume-equated, with less time). A drop is short, lighter and done fatigued, so each drop is half a hard set and the drops after one top set add at most 1 set.

partials.label: Partials
partials.logging: a whole set done with partial range of motion (meant: lengthened partials). Partial reps added after a full-ROM set to failure: log them as a separate partials row.
partials.why: Partial vs full ROM differences were trivial to small, with a possible edge for partials at long muscle lengths (Wolf 2023 meta-analysis; Pedrosa 2022 knee-extension trial). Counts like a normal set when hard. Partial reps are not comparable with full reps, so no PRs.

set_tags.hard_rule: credit applies only when the set is hard (working, reps >= 1, RIR <= hardRIR or none entered). A tagged set with no RIR uses the tag default_rir.
set_tags.volume: load x reps of every tagged working set stays in logged volume (it is work done).

warmup_ramp.note: One-tap warm-ups (#5), tools/warmup.py warmup_sets. Ramp sets are kind=warmup, so they are already excluded from PRs, hard sets, volume and analytics. Percentages and reps are coaching convention [C]/[M], not measured optima. Evidence: high-load dynamic warm-ups improve strength/power performance (McCrary 2015 systematic review); no warm-up injury-prevention evidence was found there.

applies_to.accessory: only accessory_equipment exercises whose first working load is >= accessory_min_load and whose prime mover is not already warm; at most accessory_max_sets ramp sets
applies_to.isolation: never (do the first working set a touch lighter if wanted)

floor.note: no ramp when the first working load is below this (or below 1.5 x the empty bar for bar equipment): the first working set is its own warm-up

sets_by_working_load.note: kg-equivalent of the first working load

warm_muscle.rule: prime mover (rating 1.0) already trained by >= 1 done working set earlier in the session -> one feeler set only

warmup_ramp.bodyweight: exercises with bodyweight_fraction: one bodyweight-only set of 5 when the working set has added load (assisted machines: one set at 1 step more assistance x 5); otherwise none.
warmup_ramp.rounding: gym profile nearest real load (tools/loads.py nearest_real_load, ties lighter), never below the lightest load the equipment can make; ramp loads strictly increase and stay below the working load; duplicates after rounding keep the heavier-percentage set.

progress_signals.note: Per-exercise and per-muscle progress (backlog progress-signals item; tools/deload.py exercise_trends / muscle_progress). A model, not a measurement: e1RM from sets of 6-10 reps near failure moves a few percent session to session, so thresholds are wide.
progress_signals.metric: best e1RM per session (effective load, logger.prs e1RM rules: working, reps <= e1rm_max_reps, set tags excluded per set_tags.pr_exclude); deload sessions (session.deload = true) excluded
progress_signals.slope: least-squares slope of e1RM vs days, x 7, as % of the mean e1RM in the window = %/week

status.insufficient: fewer than min_sessions or span < min_span_days

progress_signals.muscle: exercises with rating >= 0.5 for the muscle; mean of their %/week weighted by rating x sessions; same thresholds

deload_signals.note: Suggested (not planned) deload (#12), tools/deload.py deload_check. Points add up to a score; the prompt appears when score >= suggest_score. A model built on coaching consensus and survey data, not a validated fatigue test, and not medical advice.

eligible.note: no prompt before ~4 weeks of logs (Chief of Staff decision, logging-spec §15.4) or within 4 weeks of the last deload

weeks_since_deload.from: end of the last history.deloads entry, else the first completed session
weeks_since_deload.why: surveyed strength/physique athletes deload about every 5.6 +/- 2.3 weeks (Rogerson 2024); Delphi coaches describe pre-planned deloads every 4-8 weeks (Bell 2023). Time alone reaches the threshold only at 10 weeks.

performance.rule: over progress_signals.window_weeks: >= min_lifts exercises with a trend; 2 points if >= dropping_share of them are dropping, else 1 point if >= stalled_or_dropping_share are stalled or dropping
performance.why: athletes report deloading when performance stalls (Rogerson 2024). Plateaus have many causes, so this alone does not trigger a prompt.

rir_drift.rule: a recent working set (last 14 days) at the same load (+/-1%) with the same or fewer reps but a LOWER logged RIR than the most recent earlier set at that load -> drift event; >= 2 exercises with an event -> 1 point. Both RIRs must be logged.
rir_drift.caveat: Mr Dude trains most sets to failure (RIR 0), so drift is rarely visible; the e1RM trend carries that information instead.

hard_sets_over_target.rule: the last 3 completed weeks each had >= 2 muscles above targets.json max (completed_analytics hard sets, credited)

readiness.rule: history.readiness [{date, score 1-5 (5 = fresh)}]: mean of the last 7 days <= 2.5 with >= 3 entries -> 1 point (covers soreness and joint aches, which athletes report as deload triggers, Rogerson 2024)

choices.use: Use it: start the deload version for deload_version.days_length days (history.deloads gets {start, end, source:"suggested"})
choices.later: Ask me later: snooze 1 day (asked again at the next app launch after 24 h)

prompt.copy: Signs point to a lighter week: <top reasons>. This is a suggestion from your logs, not a diagnosis.

deload_version.load_rule: last working load x 0.9, rounded DOWN to a real load (loads.py nearest_real_load mode down); bodyweight exercises keep bodyweight and drop added load by the same factor
deload_version.sessions: logged with session.deload = true: excluded from progress signals and deload trends; PRs and analytics still count them
deload_version.why: Delphi coaches agreed deloads can reduce volume (fewer sets), proximity to failure and intensity, keep familiar exercises and frequency (Bell 2023); athletes report fewer sets and reps, lighter loads and more RIR, same frequency and exercises (Rogerson 2024).

deload_signals.evidence_note: Honest status: deloading is mostly expert opinion. The Bell 2023 Delphi panel itself agreed "there are limited scientific studies and understanding about deloading" (100%) and that current approaches rest on coach experience. The one trial of a mid-programme deload (Coleman 2024: 1 week off training at the midpoint of a 9-week programme, 39 resistance-trained adults) found no difference in muscle growth and slightly smaller lower-body strength gains than training straight through. No study has validated these triggers or thresholds; they are our model of what coaches and athletes report. Treat the prompt as a nudge to consider a lighter week, not a measurement of fatigue.
deload_signals.evidence_short: Several of your fatigue signals are up. A lighter week is worth considering, but deload triggers are coach experience, not tested science.

review.on_plan_margin_note: A muscle is on plan when credited done >= planned - margin, in credited sets. Mid-week, planned = routine sets Monday through today.
review.flat_pct_note: Finish-summary arrow is flat when the top-set e1RM (or volume) changes by no more than this percent.
review.block_min_prior_weeks_note: Block comparison stays hidden until the prior window has at least this many weeks with logs (on top of the Phase E gate).
review.block_exclude_deload_note: 4 wk vs Prev skips weeks that contain a deload session (same rule as progress_signals). Each window reaches back over skipped weeks to keep window_weeks training weeks; block_min_prior_weeks still applies. Show 'deload excluded' when a week was skipped.
review.block_exclude_current_week_note: 4 wk vs Prev skips the in-progress week (a partial week would read as a drop). Windows reach back to keep window_weeks completed training weeks. Show 'This week is in progress and not counted'.

swap_tags.description: Tag vocabulary for exercise-swap difference lines. Each exercise in exercises.json carries swap attributes; an alternative's difference lines come from comparing its attributes with the current exercise's.

evidence_levels.supported: Mainstream training-study evidence; citations listed and checked.
evidence_levels.biomechanics: Follows from clear mechanics (equipment guidance, one limb at a time, where the load sits). No study needed for the description itself.
evidence_levels.modeled: Coach consensus. Plausible and common in practice, but not shown in controlled studies. Treat as a model, not a finding.

vocabulary.label: Stretch emphasis
vocabulary.meaning: How much the main muscle is loaded at long length (in the stretch). 3 = hardest near the stretch, 1 = hardest near the squeeze.

vocabulary.label: Triceps long-head bias
vocabulary.meaning: Arm overhead, so the triceps long head works from a stretched position.

vocabulary.label: Biceps long-head stretch
vocabulary.meaning: Arm behind the body, which lengthens the biceps long head at the bottom. Mechanics are clear. A 2026 MRI study (Kobayashi 2026) found incline curls grew the biceps more than preacher curls, but the long head was not measured separately.

vocabulary.label: Brachialis & brachioradialis bias
vocabulary.meaning: More of the elbow-flexing work goes to the brachialis and brachioradialis: a neutral (hammer) or overhand (reverse) forearm puts the biceps at a mechanical disadvantage, and on a preacher pad the upper arm sits in front of the body, which slackens the biceps long head. Hammer and reverse curls: biomechanics. Preacher curls: supported, but only against incline curls (Kobayashi 2026); a straight comparison with standing curls has not been tested.

evidence_overrides.note: Kobayashi 2026 (MRI, 12 weeks): dumbbell preacher curls grew the brachialis and brachioradialis more than incline curls, while incline curls grew the biceps more and total elbow-flexor growth was similar. Machine and cable preacher curls share the arm position. Evidence is preacher vs incline only.

vocabulary.label: Upper-chest bias
vocabulary.meaning: An incline bench or a low-to-high path presses up and in, in line with the upper (clavicular) chest fibres. Incline presses: supported (Chaves 2020: more upper-chest thickness after incline than flat pressing; small study in untrained men). Incline flies, low-to-high cable flies and angled landmine presses: biomechanics.

evidence_overrides.note: Chaves 2020: incline barbell pressing grew upper-chest muscle thickness more than flat pressing (8 weeks, untrained men, once a week). Dumbbell, Smith and machine incline presses use the same angle.

vocabulary.label: Lower-chest bias
vocabulary.meaning: A decline bench, dips or a high-to-low cable path bring the arms down and in, in line with the lower (sternal and costal) chest fibres. Mechanics and EMG only; no growth study compares them with flat pressing.

vocabulary.label: Rectus femoris bias
vocabulary.meaning: Knee extension with the hip open, so the two-joint rectus femoris (front of the thigh) does a big share. Leg extensions: supported (Zabaleta-Korta 2021: leg extensions grew the rectus femoris, Smith squats did not; Kubo 2019: squats did not grow it). Sissy squats: biomechanics (hip stays extended while the knee bends).

evidence_overrides.note: Zabaleta-Korta 2021: leg extensions grew the rectus femoris in all measured regions, Smith-machine squats did not. Kubo 2019: full and half squats did not grow the rectus femoris.

vocabulary.label: Gastrocnemius bias (knee straight)
vocabulary.meaning: Calf raise with the knee straight, so the two-joint gastrocnemius stays long and does a big share. Kinoshita 2023: standing raises grew the gastrocnemius far more than seated raises, and the soleus grew about the same with both, so there is no separate soleus tag.

vocabulary.label: Glute bias
vocabulary.meaning: A squat or leg-press setup that shifts work from the quads toward the glutes: feet high on the platform, or facing the pad with the hips pushed back. Mechanics (more hip bend, less knee bend); growth has not been compared directly.

vocabulary.label: Lower-back focus
vocabulary.meaning: A back extension where the lower back (spinal erectors) is the main target: the spine bends and straightens, or the pad sits so the hips barely move. A hip extension that keeps the spine still (45-degree glute hyperextension, reverse hyper, hip thrust) puts the work on the glutes and hamstrings instead.

vocabulary.label: Wrist-extensor focus (back of forearm)
vocabulary.meaning: The wrist bends back against the load (palms down), so the extensors on the back of the forearm move it. A palms-up wrist curl and most grip work load the flexors on the palm side instead. The library rates the forearm as one region, so this tag carries the split.

vocabulary.label: More hip-flexor work (legs lift)
vocabulary.meaning: The legs are raised or held up, so the hip flexors do much of the lifting while the abs control the pelvis. A crunch curls the spine with the legs still.

vocabulary.label: Shoulders pulled down and back
vocabulary.meaning: Hang type: you actively pull the shoulder blades down and back and hold or move them there (active hang, scapular pull-up), rather than hanging relaxed (dead hang), shrugging them up, or pulling with the arms.

vocabulary.label: Lat width focus
vocabulary.meaning: Wide overhand vertical pull, elbows out to the side. Coaches use it for upper lats and teres; the lat is one muscle, so this is a tendency.

vocabulary.label: Upper-back thickness focus
vocabulary.meaning: Horizontal row that hits the mid-back (rhomboids, mid traps, rear delts) as much as or more than the lats. A row without it is more lat-focused, shown as "Less upper-back focus".

vocabulary.label: More upper-trap work
vocabulary.meaning: Heavy shoulder elevation or upward rotation, or holding heavy loads at the sides, so the upper traps work hard.

vocabulary.label: Peak-contraction focus
vocabulary.meaning: Hardest at the fully shortened position (the squeeze). Popular for mind-muscle work; no growth advantage shown.

vocabulary.label: Isolation
vocabulary.meaning: How well the move keeps the work on one target muscle. 3 = supported single-joint, 1 = multi-joint compound.

vocabulary.label: Stability
vocabulary.meaning: How much the equipment balances the load for you. Machines, cables and Smith 3, free weights 2, rings, suspension and single-leg free weights 1.

vocabulary.label: One side at a time
vocabulary.meaning: Works one arm or leg at a time: evens out sides, needs more time per set.

vocabulary.label: Independent arm levers
vocabulary.meaning: Machine with a separate lever for each arm (iso-lateral): each side moves its own load, and one arm can work alone.

vocabulary.label: Static hold
vocabulary.meaning: Held position (isometric) rather than reps through a range of motion.

vocabulary.label: Leg drive helps the press
vocabulary.meaning: A short knee dip and drive start the weight, so more load moves overhead than in a strict press.

vocabulary.label: Systemic fatigue
vocabulary.meaning: Whole-body fatigue per hard set (breathing, bracing, recovery cost). Coach consensus, tied to the existing fatigue field.

vocabulary.label: Loads the spine
vocabulary.meaning: The spine carries the load (bar on the back or overhead, heavy bent-over or hinge positions, heavy carries).

vocabulary.label: Loading potential
vocabulary.meaning: How much absolute load you can use and progress over time. 3 = big compound lifts, 1 = light isolation or bodyweight-only.

vocabulary.label: Steadier cable tension
vocabulary.meaning: A cable keeps resistance on through more of the range than gravity-loaded free weights.

vocabulary.label: Skill demand
vocabulary.meaning: How much technique or practice the lift needs before it can be trained hard with consistent technique.

vocabulary.label: Load in front, more upright torso
vocabulary.meaning: The load sits in front of the body (bar on the front of the shoulders, a bell or bar end at the chest), so the torso stays more upright than with a bar on the back. Gullett 2009 and Yavuz 2015 (context references, EMG and kinematics) found less trunk lean and similar or slightly higher quad activity; no growth study, so the line names the posture only.

vocabulary.label: Dead-stop reps (reset on the floor)
vocabulary.meaning: Every rep starts from the floor at a dead stop, with no bounce out of the bottom, and you reset your position between reps.

vocabulary.label: Finishes overhead
vocabulary.meaning: Each rep ends with the arms locked out overhead (relative to the torso): overhead presses, the snatch, the get-up and the windmill. Angled landmine presses and a clean to the rack do not.

vocabulary.label: Anti-rotation (resist twisting)
vocabulary.meaning: The trunk holds still while the load tries to twist it, rather than curling or rotating against it.

levels.2: about shoulder width, or not grip-specific

vocabulary.label: Grip width
vocabulary.meaning: How far apart the hands are on a bar or handle. 1 = close (V-handle, close-grip bar), 2 = about shoulder width or not grip-specific, 3 = wide. EMG studies (Andersen 2014, Lusk 2010; context references) found that grip width changes lat activity little, so the line describes the grip, not a growth difference.

vocabulary.label: Neutral grip (palms facing in)
vocabulary.meaning: Palms face each other (hammer grip, V-handle, neutral handles). Many people prefer it; that is a preference, not a finding.

vocabulary.label: More grip demand
vocabulary.meaning: Grip (forearms) is a real limit on load or reps.

maeo2021.authors: Maeo S, Huang M, Wu Y, et al.
maeo2021.title: Greater Hamstrings Muscle Hypertrophy but Similar Damage Protection after Training at Long versus Short Muscle Lengths
maeo2021.finding: Seated (hip-flexed) leg curl grew the hamstrings more than prone (lying) leg curl.

maeo2023.authors: Maeo S, Wu Y, Huang M, et al.
maeo2023.title: Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position
maeo2023.finding: Overhead cable extensions grew the triceps (most of all the long head) more than pushdowns.

pedrosa2022.authors: Pedrosa GF, Lima FV, Schoenfeld BJ, et al.
pedrosa2022.title: Partial range of motion training elicits favorable improvements in muscular adaptations when carried out at long muscle lengths
pedrosa2022.finding: Leg extension partials at long quad lengths grew the quads more than partials at short lengths.

kassiano2023.authors: Kassiano W, Costa B, Kunevaliki G, et al.
kassiano2023.title: Greater Gastrocnemius Muscle Hypertrophy After Partial Range of Motion Training Performed at Long Muscle Lengths
kassiano2023.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
kassiano2023.finding: Calf-raise partials in the stretched range grew the gastrocnemius more than partials at short lengths.

sato2021.authors: Sato S, Yoshida R, Kiyono R, et al.
sato2021.title: Elbow Joint Angles in Elbow Flexor Unilateral Resistance Exercise Training Determine Its Effects on Muscle Strength and Thickness of Trained and Non-trained Arms
sato2021.finding: Preacher curls in the extended-elbow (long-length) range grew the elbow flexors more than the flexed range.

wolf2023.authors: Wolf M, Androulakis-Korakakis P, Fisher J, Schoenfeld B, Steele J
wolf2023.title: Partial Vs Full Range of Motion Resistance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
wolf2023.journal: International Journal of Strength and Conditioning
wolf2023.finding: Across studies, training at long muscle lengths tends to match or modestly beat full range for growth; the effect is small and uncertain.

chaves2020.authors: Chaves SFN, Rocha-Júnior VA, Encarnação IGA, et al.
chaves2020.title: Effects of Horizontal and Incline Bench Press on Neuromuscular Adaptations in Untrained Young Men
chaves2020.finding: Untrained men, 8 weeks, once a week, equal sets: the incline bench press grew upper-chest muscle thickness (second intercostal site) more than the flat press; the other sites and strength gains did not differ. Small study; ultrasound muscle thickness.

kobayashi2026.authors: Kobayashi Y, Maeo S, Eihara Y, et al.
kobayashi2026.title: Exercise-specific preferential hypertrophy of individual elbow flexor muscles after incline versus preacher dumbbell curl training
kobayashi2026.finding: MRI, 12 weeks, one arm each way: preacher curls grew the brachialis and brachioradialis more than incline curls, incline curls grew the biceps more; total elbow-flexor growth was similar. Compared with incline curls only.

kinoshita2023.authors: Kinoshita M, Maeo S, Kobayashi Y, et al.
kinoshita2023.title: Triceps surae muscle hypertrophy is greater after standing versus seated calf-raise training
kinoshita2023.finding: Standing (knee straight) calf raises grew the gastrocnemius far more than seated (knee bent) raises; soleus growth was similar in both.

zabaletakorta2021.authors: Zabaleta-Korta A, Fernández-Peña E, Torres-Unda J, et al.
zabaletakorta2021.title: The role of exercise selection in regional Muscle Hypertrophy: A randomized controlled trial
zabaletakorta2021.finding: With equal volume and intensity, leg extensions grew the rectus femoris in all measured regions, while Smith-machine squats did not.

kubo2019.authors: Kubo K, Ikebukuro T, Yata H
kubo2019.title: Effects of squat training with different depths on lower limb muscle volumes
kubo2019.finding: Full and half squats grew the vasti similarly and neither grew the rectus femoris (MRI, 10 weeks).

gullett2009.authors: Gullett JC, Tillman MD, Gutierrez GM, Chow JW
gullett2009.title: A Biomechanical Comparison of Back and Front Squats in Healthy Trained Individuals
gullett2009.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
gullett2009.finding: EMG and kinetics, 15 trained lifters: muscle activity was similar in front and back squats; the back squat had higher knee compressive forces and knee extensor moments. Not a growth study.

yavuz2015.authors: Yavuz HU, Erdağ D, Amca AM, Aritan S
yavuz2015.title: Kinematic and EMG activities during front and back squat variations in maximum loads
yavuz2015.finding: EMG and kinematics at maximal loads, 12 lifters: more trunk lean in the back squat; vastus medialis EMG was higher in the front squat and semitendinosus EMG higher in the back squat on the way up. Not a growth study.

nunes2020.authors: Nunes JP, Jacinto JL, Ribeiro AS, et al.
nunes2020.title: Placing Greater Torque at Shorter or Longer Muscle Lengths? Effects of Cable vs. Barbell Preacher Curl Training on Muscular Strength and Hypertrophy in Young Adults
nunes2020.journal: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
nunes2020.finding: Cable (short-length torque) and barbell (long-length torque) preacher curls gave similar biceps growth. This is why peak_contraction_focus stays modeled.

andersen2014.authors: Andersen V, Fimland MS, Wiik E, Skoglund A, Saeterbakken AH
andersen2014.title: Effects of Grip Width on Muscle Strength and Activation in the Lat Pull-Down
andersen2014.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
andersen2014.finding: EMG: narrow, medium and wide overhand pulldown grips gave similar lat activation; the wide grip allowed slightly less load.

lusk2010.authors: Lusk SJ, Hale BD, Russell DM
lusk2010.title: Grip Width and Forearm Orientation Effects on Muscle Activity During the Lat Pull-Down
lusk2010.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
lusk2010.finding: EMG: an overhand pulldown grip gave slightly more lat activation than an underhand grip; grip width made no difference.

compare.ordinal: If alt[tag] > cur[tag], show label_higher; if lower, show label_lower; if equal, nothing.
compare.flag: If the flag is on the alternative only, show label; if on the current exercise only, show label_lost; if on both or neither, nothing.
compare.order: Sort candidate lines by the tag priority (1 first). Muscle-specific tags come first (stretch, long heads, brachialis, upper and lower chest, rectus femoris, gastrocnemius, glutes, lower back, wrist extensors, hip flexors, active shoulders, lat width, upper back, traps, peak), then isolation, stability, side, independent arms, holds and leg drive, then fatigue, spine, loading, tension and skill, then the set-up lines (front-loaded, dead-stop reps, overhead finish, anti-rotation), and last the grip lines (width, neutral grip, grip demand), which describe the grip rather than a muscle difference.
compare.empty: If no tag differs and both exercises have swap attributes, show empty_line once instead of difference lines (the swap list still shows the existing short tags).
compare.empty_line: Very similar to your current exercise
compare.missing: A custom exercise without swap attributes gets no difference lines.
compare.disclaimer: Tags describe how an exercise usually loads muscles, not what any one person will feel or grow. No medical claims.

swap_tags.evidence_overrides: Optional per-tag list [{level, exercises, citations, note}]. The tag's `evidence` is the level for every exercise not listed (its floor); a listed exercise carries `level`, backed by the listed citations. Use tools/swaptags.py tag_evidence(tag, exercise_id).

ranking.description: One shared suggestion ranking model for swaps, the exercise tray, empty-workout suggestions and preset slot filling. Model choices, not measurements. Spec: data/ranking-spec.md.
ranking.evidence_levels: Same as swap_tags.evidence_levels: supported (checked citations), biomechanics, modeled.
ranking.scale: Every term is a 0-1 (or -1..1) quantity times a weight on the same scale as fit (0-1). score = sum of weighted terms, unclamped, rounded to 4 decimals. Most sit between 0 and 1; only sort with it, never show it as a percentage.

primary.label: Main muscle groups
primary.note: chest; shoulders (front, side, rear delts); arms (biceps, triceps); back (lats, upper back); quads; hamstrings; glutes.

accessory.label: Accessory groups
accessory.note: traps, forearms, abs, obliques, calves, adductors, abductors, lower back. The app has no neck muscle; a future neck id belongs here.

groups.use: Default priority G[m]. Used by the priority term in tray and empty_workout (in swap and preset the muscle is already fixed, so G is flattened to 1). Goals multiply it, bias lifts a biased muscle to at least bias.priority_floor.

muscle_size.label: Size
muscle_size.meaning: Build muscle across the whole body. This matches the app's default targets.

evidence_notes.stretch_emphasis: supported: training at long muscle lengths tends to grow muscle as much or more (swap_tags stretch_emphasis citations).
evidence_notes.stability: modeled: stable options let you train closer to failure with less setup and balance cost.
evidence_notes.systemic_fatigue: modeled: more stimulus per unit of whole-body fatigue.
evidence_notes.reps: none: logger.rep_range_by_type is already a hypertrophy range.

strength.label: Strength
strength.meaning: Get stronger on the big lifts: heavier, lower-rep work on compounds you can load and progress.

evidence_notes.reps: supported: heavier loads give larger 1RM gains (schoenfeld2017load).
evidence_notes.loading_potential: supported in direction (heavy loading drives 1RM); the 0.6 weight is modeled.
evidence_notes.muscle_priority: modeled: prime movers of squat, bench, deadlift and row get a small raise.

joint_friendly.label: Longevity & joint-friendly
joint_friendly.meaning: Train for the long haul: stable, easy-to-learn options, less spinal loading and moderate loads in higher rep ranges.

evidence_notes.reps: supported for growth: lighter loads taken close to failure grow muscle about as well as heavy loads (schoenfeld2017load). Choosing them for this goal is a training preference (modeled); no joint or injury outcome is claimed.
evidence_notes.attr_pref: modeled: preference, not a safety rating.
evidence_notes.spinal_cap_factor: modeled: spinal-load session and week caps (rules spinal_load) are scaled by 0.75 for scoring.
evidence_notes.disclaimer: Not medical advice and not a treatment or injury-prevention claim.

maintain.label: Maintain
maintain.meaning: Keep what you have built on less training time: far fewer sets, but keep the weights heavy.

evidence_notes.volume: supported: far less volume keeps muscle and strength if load stays high (young adults kept size on 1/3 and 1/9 of the volume, bickel2011; spiering2021). The app uses 1/2 of the minimum as a cushion because older lifters needed more (bickel2011). The exact 0.5 is modeled.
evidence_notes.loading_potential: supported in direction: intensity is the key variable to keep (spiering2021); weight modeled.

aesthetic_v_taper.label: Upper-body width & arms
aesthetic_v_taper.meaning: Emphasize shoulder width, back width and arms.

evidence_notes.muscle_priority: modeled: a visual-proportion preference, not a health or performance claim.

aesthetic_v_taper.label_note: Often called "masculine aesthetics". Anyone can pick it.

aesthetic_lower_emphasis.label: Glutes, legs & shoulder shape
aesthetic_lower_emphasis.meaning: Emphasize glutes, legs and rounded shoulders, with less upper-trap work.

evidence_notes.muscle_priority: modeled: a visual-proportion preference, not a health or performance claim.

aesthetic_lower_emphasis.label_note: Often called "feminine aesthetics". Anyone can pick it.

conditioning.label: Fat loss & conditioning
conditioning.meaning: Keep muscle while dieting and build work capacity: quick-to-set-up, low-skill options and moderate-to-high reps.

evidence_notes.fat_loss: Fat loss comes from diet; the app does not model calories or cardio.
evidence_notes.volume: modeled: minimums kept to hold on to muscle, maximums trimmed 10% because recovery is usually worse in a calorie deficit.
evidence_notes.reps: supported for growth across rep ranges (schoenfeld2017load); the conditioning benefit of higher reps is modeled.

goal_attrs.flag_value: x = 1 if the flag is in swap.flags else 0

pseudo.type_primary: x = 1 if exercise type is primary else 0

goal_attrs.goal_score: a_g(c) = clamp(sum_k attr_pref[g][k] * x_k(c), -1, 1). Missing swap block (custom) -> 0.

goal_combine.muscle_priority: M[m] = arithmetic mean over selected goals of muscle_priority[m] (missing = 1.0).
goal_combine.attr: A(c) = mean over selected goals of a_g(c).
goal_combine.rep_range_by_type: Per type, goals with a range vote; low = round(mean of lows), high = round(mean of highs) (half up). No vote -> logger.rep_range_by_type.
goal_combine.volume: Vmin[m], Vmax[m] = mean over goals of volume factors. Exception: maintain + any other goal = specialization; muscles with M[m] > 1 use the mean of the other goals, all others use maintain's factors.
goal_combine.no_goals: M = 1, A = 0, V = 1, logger rep ranges: identical to the current app.

goal_conflicts.message: Strength wants heavy, low-rep sets with long rests; conditioning wants higher reps and shorter rests. Rep ranges are averaged. If conditioning means a lot of extra cardio, expect some interference with strength gains, more so with running and with longer, more frequent sessions.
Strength favors heavy barbell lifts; joint-friendly favors stable, lower-spinal-load options. Exercise preferences are averaged and the stricter spinal cap applies.

Maintain lowers volume, muscle size wants full volume. Treated as specialization: only muscles your other goals prioritize keep full volume. With muscle size alone nothing is prioritized, so maintain volume applies everywhere.
Maintain lowers volume. Strength-priority muscles keep strength volume; the rest drop to maintenance.

conflict_penalty.rule: With 2+ goals, an exercise gets -0.03 when one goal scores it a_g >= 0.5 and another a_g <= -0.5 (it fits one goal and clearly fights another).

targets.rule: min'[m] = round_half(min[m] * levelMinFactor[level] * Vmin[m] * clamp(M[m], 0.85, 1.2)); max'[m] = round_half(max[m] * Vmax[m] * clamp(M[m], 1.0, 1.2)); min' <= 0.8 * max'.
targets.floor: floor[m] = round_half(min[m] * levelMinFactor.beginner * Vmin[m]): nothing is ever traded below the beginner-level minimum (scaled by goal volume).

bias.ids: Any exercises.json muscles id, or a regions id (map region, e.g. chest_upper, triceps_long). A region biases its parent muscle (regionGroup) for targets and its own head rating for exercises.

target_raise.cap: max'' <= round_half(max[m] * Vmax[m] * volume_bands.red_factor) (the red line); min'' <= 0.8 * max''.

trade_off.rule: added = sum over biased muscles of (min'' - min'). Lower the min of non-biased muscles with M[m] <= 1 by up to `added` in total, accessory group first, then primary, each in proportion to its slack (min' - floor), on the 0.5 grid, never below floor. If slack runs out the remainder stays (reported as untraded). Max values of other muscles and the session hard-set and spinal caps never change.

bias.priority_floor_note: Only for muscle ids. A region bias (e.g. chest_upper) raises its parent muscle's targets but works on exercises through the bias term only, so every chest exercise is not lifted alike.

exercise_boost.rule: x(c) = max over bias ids b of [0.8 * clamp((r_b(c) - 0.5) / 0.5, 0, 1) + 0.2 * flag_b(c)]; r_b = heads[b] for a region, muscles[b] for a muscle. term = W_bias * x.

related_pattern.rule: Swap only: when a bias id belongs to the current exercise's main muscle, a candidate whose legacy pattern (rules.patterns) differs from the current one but that shares its patterns.json main slot (patterns[0]) and has a higher r_b than the current exercise is treated as same-pattern: +0.4 fit (the swap.json same-pattern term, 40/100). Lets an upper-chest bias surface incline presses when swapping a flat press. Never applies without a bias, so neutral swaps are unchanged.

favorites.rule: A favorite gets +0.10. Because the boost is additive and equal to the margin, a favorite can only pass an option whose score without favorites is higher by less than 0.10, never one that fits the context better by more. Hard constraints are applied before scoring, so a favorite that is excluded, unavailable or already on that day is never shown.

hard_constraints.rule: An exercise whose equipment_needs the active gym profile cannot meet is removed (see equipment). Unknown items stay, with note equipment_unknown.
An exercise already on that day is removed (swap, tray, empty_workout, preset). The swapped tile itself is never a candidate.
swap: same as tools/swap.py (cosine >= 0.6 or same legacy pattern).
preset: patterns.py candidates(slot, level) (counts for the slot, level filters). empty_workout: the same level filters on the whole library, non-custom only.

equipment.rule: status(profile, equipment, exercise_id): 1) profile.equipment[equipment] true/false if present (optional field: {equipment name: bool}); 2) bodyweight -> available; 3) barbell, trap bar, smith machine, landmine, plate-loaded machine: plates [] -> unavailable, bars[eq] null -> unavailable, bars has eq and plates non-empty -> available, else unknown; 4) dumbbell/kettlebell: list present and empty -> unavailable, non-empty -> available, absent -> unknown; 5) machine/cable: stacks[exercise_id] or stacks[eq] present -> available, stacks[eq] null -> unavailable, else unknown; 6) anything else (rings, suspension, band, medicine ball, stability ball) -> unknown.
equipment.no_profile: logger.gym_profile_default[prefs.unit or lb], the same default suggestions use.
equipment.unknown: allowed, with note equipment_unknown so the UI can say "Check your gym has this".
equipment.profile_field_added: gym profile gets an optional `equipment` map {token: bool} keyed by rules.equipment_items tokens (legacy equipment names such as rings or barbell still work in equipment_status); nothing else in gym_profile_schema changes.

needs.rule: needs_status(profile, exercise): if the profile has no (or an empty) equipment map, or the exercise has no equipment_needs (custom), use status(profile, exercise.equipment, id) above, unchanged. Otherwise every item of exercise.equipment_needs must be met: an item "a|b" is available if any token is available, unavailable if all are unavailable, else unknown. Token status: equipment[token] true -> available, false -> unavailable; else available if a true token implies it (equipment_items.items[t].implies); else, for tokens with a legacy equipment name, the loads-field status of that name (plates: plates list non-empty/empty); else unknown (also for tokens outside the vocabulary). Exercise: unavailable if any item is unavailable (removed), else unknown if any item is unknown (kept, note equipment_unknown), else available. [] = available.

priority.rule: P[m] = G[m] * M[m] (G = 1 in swap and preset), raised to >= bias.priority_floor for biased muscles. prio(c) = sum r_m P[m] / sum r_m over muscles with r_m >= 0.25. term = W_priority * clamp((prio(c) - 1) / 0.25, -1, 1).

gap.rule: Week totals use the planner counting (sets x rating, ratings >= 0.25) over the whole board, minus the swapped tile. For each muscle the candidate trains (r >= 0.25), add = sets x r; deficit = min' - week; total = week + add. Over-target bands come from rules.volume_bands: amber = total > max', red = total > max' * red_factor. u = clamp(deficit / full_at, 0, 1) if deficit > 0; else -1 if red; else -0.5 * clamp((total - max') / full_at, 0, 1) if amber; else 0. need(c) = sum r u / sum r. term = W_gap * need (bonus and penalty share the weight).

theme.rule: Day theme (tray and empty_workout only; weight 0 in swap and preset so neutral parity stays exact). Muscles already credited that day (all tiles on the day, planner counting): t[m] = clamp(day[m] / session.solid[m], 0, 1). theme(c) = sum r_m t[m] / sum r_m over the candidate's muscles with r >= 0.25. term = W_theme * theme.
theme.sizing: W_theme = 0.08. A real weekly gap (a muscle at least 2 credited sets under min', the amber/red-under line in targets.counting) on a single-muscle exercise gives gap >= 0.5 x W_gap = 0.125 (tray) / 0.15 (empty_workout), more than the largest possible theme term, so theme never beats a real gap. It is enough to put leg work above chest isolation on a full legs day.

prefatigue.rule: Earlier tiles in the session (swap: tiles before the swapped one; tray/empty/preset: all tiles already on that day). For the candidate's target muscles (r >= 0.5): pf = sum r * clamp(pre[m] / session.heavy[m], 0, 1) / sum r, times type weight (primary 1, accessory 0.75, isolation 0.5). term = -W_prefatigue * pf.

systemic.rule: frac = clamp(sets already done before this slot that day (swap: earlier tiles; tray/empty/preset: all tiles on the day) / session_hard_sets.warn_above[level], 0, 1). term = -W_systemic * frac * (systemic_fatigue - 2): low-fatigue options gain, high-fatigue ones lose, as the session fills up.

spinal.rule: cap = spinal_load.session_warn_above[level] * spinal_cap_factor. frac = clamp(heavy squat + hinge sets already done before this slot that day / cap, 0, 1). term = +W_spinal/2 * frac without the spinal_load flag, -W_spinal/2 * frac with it. Extra -W_spinal when the candidate is a heavy squat or hinge and its sets plus the heavy sets on all other tiles that day would push the session past cap or the week past spinal_load.week_warn_above[level] * spinal_cap_factor.
spinal.evidence: modeled (counts and caps reuse rules spinal_load)
spinal.reason_note: The "Less spinal load after ..." reason is shown only for exercises that train one of reason_muscles at >= 0.5 (where a spinal-loading option was a real alternative); the score term applies to all.

coverage.rule: Slot counts for the week (check_program.slot_counts, minus the swapped tile). For each slot the candidate counts toward: 1 if the slot is in patterns.required and at 0, 0.5 if below weekly_min_by_level[level], else 0; take the max. term = W_coverage * value.

favorite.rule: term = favorites.boost if the id is a favorite.

swap.fit: tools/swap.py score(current, candidate) / 100 (+ bias.related_pattern when it applies).
swap.pool: every exercise passing swap eligibility (custom exercises allowed, as in swap.py)

tray.fit: 0.5 for every exercise (the tray shows everything; context decides the order).
tray.pool: the exercises that pass the tray's own search and filters

empty_workout.fit: patterns.json slot score of the exercise for its main slot (first slot it can count for) / 100, with the board; 0.3 if it counts for no slot.
empty_workout.pool: whole library, non-custom, patterns.py level filters, not already on that day

preset.fit: patterns.json slot score for the given slot / 100 (patterns.py _score with the partial board).
preset.note: Used when a preset is built for someone with goals, bias or favorites. Shipped presets are not regenerated.

ranking.formula: score(c) = fit(c) + W_priority*priority + W_goal*A(c) + W_bias*x(c) + W_gap*need(c) + W_theme*theme(c) - W_prefatigue*pf(c) + systemic(c) + spinal(c) + W_coverage*cov(c) + favorite(c) - conflict(c), after hard constraints.
tie_break: context tie_break (id, or library order for tray)
ranking.neutral: No goals, bias, favorites or board state: every term but fit is 0, so swap order = tools/swap.py swaps() exactly and preset order = patterns.py slot_recommendations() exactly. Tray neutral = library order except that exercises training only accessory groups drop (priority term), and empty_workout neutral = ranked by main-slot quality, then priority.

reasons.rule: Collect terms with a positive contribution >= 0.01, sort by contribution (desc), keep the top 2 as reason strings. If none, use the fit reason. Penalties are never shown as reasons.

strings.systemic: Lower fatigue for a long session

reasons.fill: {a} = "an" before a vowel sound (a, e, i, o, u), else "a"; {muscle} = app muscle label (id with spaces, lower case); {target} = region name (heat.js RNAME) or muscle label; {slot} = patterns.json slot name, lower case; {goal} = goal short label; {exercise} = name of the other session tile with the most heavy squat/hinge sets.

schoenfeld2017load.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Grgic J, Ogborn D, Krieger JW
schoenfeld2017load.title: Strength and Hypertrophy Adaptations Between Low- vs. High-Load Resistance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
schoenfeld2017load.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
schoenfeld2017load.finding: 21 studies, sets to failure: heavier loads (>60% 1RM) gave larger 1RM strength gains; muscle growth was similar across light and heavy loads.

bickel2011.authors: Bickel CS, Cross JM, Bamman MM
bickel2011.title: Exercise Dosing to Retain Resistance Training Adaptations in Young and Older Adults
bickel2011.finding: After 16 weeks of training, 32 weeks at one-third or one-ninth of the volume (same 8-12RM intensity) kept the muscle gained in young adults (one-third even added some); older adults (60-75) lost myofiber size on both doses. Strength was largely kept.

spiering2021.authors: Spiering BA, Mujika I, Sharp MA, Foulis SA
spiering2021.title: Maintaining Physical Performance: The Minimal Dose of Exercise Needed to Preserve Endurance and Strength Over Time
spiering2021.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
spiering2021.finding: Narrative review: in younger people strength and muscle size held for up to 32 weeks on as little as 1 session a week and 1 set per exercise, if relative load stayed high; older people may need 2 sessions and 2-3 sets. Intensity is the key variable.

wilson2012.authors: Wilson JM, Marin PJ, Rhea MR, Wilson SMC, Loenneke JP, Anderson JC
wilson2012.title: Concurrent Training: A Meta-Analysis Examining Interference of Aerobic and Resistance Exercises
wilson2012.journal: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
wilson2012.finding: 21 studies: adding endurance work to lifting gave smaller (mostly non-significant) strength and size gains and significantly smaller power gains; the interference grew with endurance frequency and duration and was seen with running, not cycling.

ranking.shared_citations: Keys maeo2021, maeo2023, pedrosa2022, kassiano2023, sato2021, wolf2023 live in swap_tags.citations.
ranking.limits: A ranking model built from coaching judgment and a few checked studies. Weights are modeled, not measured; they order options, they do not predict growth or strength. No medical claims: joint-friendly is a preference for stable, lower-load options, not injury prevention or treatment.

not_included.athletic_power: Considered and left out: the app has a few power exercises but no velocity, plyometric or rest programming, so the goal could not change much honestly.

volume_bands.rule: under min = blue/under; min..max = in range; total > max = amber; total > max*red_factor = red (weekly_volume warn).
volume_bands.note: Single source of truth for over-target colours. The volume panel, the body map week colours (targets.json gradient.week) and the weekly_volume rule all read this key. Decided by Chief of Staff 2026-10-21.

stretch_check.note: r2fix 2026-10-22. Per-muscle stretch check: a checked muscle passes when the week includes at least one exercise from rules.stretch_biased[muscle]; otherwise rules[missing_stretch] flags it as warn (it stays info for measure-only muscles). Checked = muscles with direct lengthened-training evidence in education/references.json; the others show the stretch share as a measure only. Models, not measurements.

hamstrings.why: Seated leg curls (hamstrings longer) grew the hamstrings more than lying leg curls.

calves.why: Straight-knee calf raises grew the gastrocnemius far more than seated raises; stretched-range partials beat top-range partials.

triceps.why: Overhead elbow extensions (long head stretched) grew the triceps more than pushdown-position extensions.

quads.why: Long-length leg-extension partials grew the quads more than short-length partials.

glutes.why: Full (deep) squats grew the glute max more than half squats. Split squats, lunges and RDLs are counted by the same long-length mechanism (modeled). Hip thrusts and bridges are not stretch-loaded; Plotkin 2023 found them similar to squats for glute growth, so they remain good glute work.

measure_only.chest: No direct long-length vs short-length growth comparison in the reference list yet.
measure_only.biceps: One study (Sato 2021, untrained, preacher-curl ranges) supports it; kept measure-only until more data.
measure_only.lats: No direct comparison in the reference list yet.

rep_ranges.note: Typical ranges, not requirements. Muscle grows across a wide span of reps when sets end close to failure; strength favors heavier loads. Pick a weight that keeps you inside the range with steady technique, and treat the ends as guides.
rep_ranges.display: display = f"{low}–{high}" + units[unit] (en dash). per_side true: the count is for each side (the app may append " / side"). not_to_failure true: end sets well before failure.

goal_notes.default: No goal picked: the app's standing ranges (rules.logger.rep_range_by_type).
goal_notes.strength: Heavier main lifts (3–6 reps; at most 6 on primary lifts) and 6–10 on accessories. Heavy loads give the most strength gain (supported: schoenfeld2017load, lopez2021). Isolation keeps the default 10–15 because it does not drive the main lifts (modeled).
goal_notes.muscle_size: Default ranges. Growth is similar across a wide range of loads when sets end close to failure (supported: schoenfeld2017load, lopez2021, schoenfeld2021rep); the middle ranges are a practical choice (modeled), not a growth threshold.
goal_notes.joint_friendly: Moderate-to-higher reps with moderate loads. Lighter loads near failure grow muscle about as well as heavy ones (supported: schoenfeld2017load, lopez2021); choosing them for this goal is a training preference (modeled). No health or injury claim is made.
goal_notes.maintain: Default ranges with the weights kept heavy; maintenance studies kept loads near 8–12RM while cutting sets (bickel2011, spiering2021).
goal_notes.aesthetic_v_taper: Default ranges; this goal changes which muscles get sets, not the reps (modeled).
goal_notes.aesthetic_lower_emphasis: Default ranges; this goal changes which muscles get sets, not the reps (modeled).
goal_notes.conditioning: Moderate-to-higher reps for denser sessions (modeled). Growth is similar across loads near failure (supported: schoenfeld2017load, lopez2021).

rep_ranges.combine: Several goals: per type, only goals that vote for that type (votes) count; low = round(mean of their lows), high = round(mean of highs), half up; no vote -> default (same rule as ranking.goal_combine.rep_range_by_type). An override with by_goal combines its goal entries the same way; goals without an entry do not vote, and no vote -> its default.
rep_ranges.per_side: Default: true when the exercise has the swap flag unilateral; an override may set it (per_side map or per_side_all).

overrides.label: Windmill

overrides.label: Turkish get-up
overrides.note: Each rep is a long multi-step movement; a few smooth reps per side.

overrides.label: Kettlebell swing
overrides.note: Ballistic: end the set while hip snap and bell height stay crisp.

overrides.label: Kettlebell clean and snatch
overrides.note: Ballistic: end the set while each rep is fast and clean.

overrides.label: Jumps and plyometrics
overrides.note: Power drills: few fast reps with full rest, never to failure; stop when height, distance or speed drops.

overrides.label: Medicine-ball throws

overrides.note: Time per set.

hypertrophy_load_range.note: Muscle growth is similar across low, moderate and high loads when sets end at or near failure.

strength_heavy.note: Heavier loads give larger strength gains; the strength goal keeps primary lifts at 6 reps or fewer.

not_to_failure.note: Power, ballistic and skill drills end before failure so each rep keeps its speed and technique (coaching convention).
