edge_cases.traps: back: trained by shrugs, rows and deadlifts and sits on the upper back; the app's splits already put shrugs on pull/back days.
edge_cases.rear_delts: shoulders: it is a deltoid head; face pulls and reverse flyes still read as shoulder work even though they are often done on back days.
edge_cases.lower_back: back: the spinal erectors run the length of the back; core here means the front and side trunk (abs, obliques).
edge_cases.forearms: arms: below the elbow, trained by curls, wrist work and grip; carries and hangs that rate forearms highest therefore show as arms.
edge_cases.glutes: legs: hip extensors trained with squats, hinges and lunges; there is no separate hips region.
edge_cases.abductors: legs: outer hip (glute medius and minimus), trained with the leg work.
edge_cases.hip_flexors: No muscle id in the library (hip-flexor work shows as the hip_flexor_work swap tag on abs exercises). A future hip_flexors id goes to core, where those exercises live.
edge_cases.neck: No muscle id in the library. A future neck id goes to back, next to traps (rules.ranking already notes where a neck id would sit).

body_regions.primary_rule: An exercise's primary region is the region of its highest-rated muscle in exercises.json muscles. Tie-breaks, in order: 1) the region with the larger sum of the exercise's muscle ratings; 2) the region of the exercise's first listed pattern (pattern_region); 3) the earlier region in order.
body_regions.tokens_note: Neutral token names only; the data sets no colors.

short_label_note: rules[].short_label: 3-5 words (a hyphenated word counts as one) for compact chips. short_label_variants keys: message_* variant names (info, week, no_pull, no_push, indirect_only), the checker ids spinal_load_session/_week as session/week, and weekly_volume over/under (sets above max / below min).

movement_patterns.derived_from: exercises.json exercises[].patterns (the patterns.json slots used by pattern_gap, test_patterns and patterns.py)
movement_patterns.rule: 1) The first slot in the exercise's patterns list that is one of the 7 compound slots, if the exercise is not type isolation (the same condition under which pattern_gap counts it for that slot). 2) Otherwise its main slot (patterns[0]) abs or carry_core -> core. 3) Main slot power -> other. 4) Any other main slot (an isolation slot: chest_fly, side_delts, biceps, glute_iso, calves, ...) -> isolation. 5) No patterns (a custom exercise without slots) -> other.
movement_patterns.why_core: core is added to the requested list because 25 library exercises (abs + carry_core slots) would otherwise sit in isolation or other, and "core" is a common tray search. power stays in other (8 exercises).

edge_cases.incline presses: horizontal_push: their main slot is horizontal_push (rules.patterns incline_press is a push pattern); upper-chest emphasis is a swap tag, not a filter.
edge_cases.landmine presses (one- and two-arm): horizontal_push: patterns lists horizontal_push first, then vertical_push; pattern_gap credits both slots, the filter shows the first.
edge_cases.jm-press: horizontal_push: main slot is triceps, but it is an accessory that pattern_gap also counts as a horizontal push, so rule 1 picks horizontal_push.
edge_cases.pullovers (dumbbell, machine, cable): isolation: main slot lat_iso; they never count as a vertical pull.
edge_cases.step-ups, split squats, lunges, pistols: lunge: main slot lunge (which also counts toward squat in pattern_gap).
edge_cases.hip thrusts and glute bridges: isolation: main slot glute_iso (a single-joint hip extension). They do not count for the hinge slot in pattern_gap, so filtering them under hinge would disagree with the checks.
edge_cases.upright row: isolation: main slot side_delts (it is multi-joint, but it fills the side-delt slot).
edge_cases.carries, get-up, Pallof press, rotations: core: main slot abs or carry_core (25 exercises, worth its own chip).
edge_cases.jumps, throws, plyometric push-up: other: main slot power; few exercises, and the equipment filter already has a Plyometric chip.
edge_cases.custom exercises: derived the same way from their patterns (patterns.custom_suggest); none -> other.

movement_patterns.consistency: For every exercise with a compound movement_pattern P, pattern_gap counts it for slot P (tested). The legacy rules.patterns map (redundant_pattern, push:pull) is unchanged; its pattern always lies inside the exercise's main slot.

analysis_metrics.note: Round 2 (2026-10-22) restructure. Every item has kind (check | measure | info), section, tab and explain {what, how, why, learn_page}. Check labels state the good condition. Flags name the days and exercises causing them (tools/analysis.py flag_details). Breakdowns per muscle and per movement pattern for stretch share, one-side share, recovery cost, stimulus per fatigue and fatigue (tools/analysis.py breakdowns). Values are models for comparing plans, not measurements. Spec: data/analysis-spec-r2.md; fixture: data/analysis-items-reference.json.

kinds.check: A rule with a pass / attention state. The label states the good condition. Counts toward checks_pass when applicable. Attention = at least one non-info flag from its rules (or, for recovery_vs_baseline, week cost above 115% of the saved baseline). Info-level flags of its rules are listed as notes and never change the state.
kinds.measure: A value or breakdown with no judgment and no state.
kinds.info: Context or an advisory note. Never counts toward checks_pass and never shows as attention. Used for model-only notes whose evidence is thin, and for info-severity rules that fire on many sound programs.

explain.how: Count of kind=check items whose applies holds (level, a saved baseline, 2+ training days) and that are in pass. 13 checks apply at every level without a saved baseline (8 board checks + 5 per-muscle stretch checks), 14 with one.
explain.why: A quick summary; the items themselves say what to look at.

items.formula: total = rules r in rules.json rules[] whose r.applies holds: level in r.applies.levels AND every r.applies.requires is met (baseline_saved: a normal-week recovery baseline is saved; training_days>=2: at least 2 days with a filled tile). pass = total minus the applicable rules with at least one non-info flag (spinal_load_session and spinal_load_week both count as spinal_load; recovery_vs_baseline fails above its warn_above, 130%). Info flags never fail a check. Only filled tiles are checked: unfilled template slots are not counted (the Builder shows them as pending). Clean board, no baseline: beginner 15/15, intermediate 14/14, advanced 14/14; with a saved baseline one more each.

items.label: Weekly sets per muscle
items.description: Effective weekly sets for each muscle against its target band, with the colour key (under / in range / over / far over), the evidence tag behind each target and the total sets in the week.

explain.what: Effective weekly sets for each muscle against its target band, with the colour key (under / in range / over / far over), the evidence tag behind each target and the total sets in the week.
explain.how: Each exercise credits sets x its rating for a muscle; ratings below 0.25 are ignored and totals round to 0.5. The band runs from the target minimum x the level factor to the target maximum; amber up to 25% over, red beyond (red_factor). The total line counts every planned set once.
explain.why: Weekly sets per muscle are the main volume lever in the cited dose-response meta-analyses; the band is a planning range, not a prescription.

items.formula: targets.json counting (fractional, min_rating_to_count, round_to); target = targets[m].min x levelMinFactor[level] .. max | rules.json volume_bands (over); under = total < level min; red = total > max x red_factor; weekly_volume rule warns on red | sum over days and tiles of sets | targets.json targets[m].evidence.tag

items.label: Every muscle within reach of its weekly range
items.description: Passes while no muscle is red: more than 2 sets under its level minimum, or more than 25% over its weekly maximum. Amber (close) passes.

explain.what: Passes while no muscle is red: more than 2 sets under its level minimum, or more than 25% over its weekly maximum. Amber (close) passes.
explain.how: weekly_volume rule on effective weekly sets per muscle. The flag names the muscle, its sets, and the exercises and days that credit it (none when the muscle gets no sets).
explain.why: Far under, the model expects little growth stimulus for that muscle; far over, little extra stimulus for the added recovery cost.

items.formula: weekly_volume rule on effective weekly sets per muscle. The flag names the muscle, its sets, and the exercises and days that credit it (none when the muscle gets no sets).

items.label: Modeled stimulus
items.description: For each muscle, the modeled share of its weekly stimulus ceiling reached by the current sets, and what one more weekly set would add.

explain.what: For each muscle, the modeled share of its weekly stimulus ceiling reached by the current sets, and what one more weekly set would add.
explain.how: S(x) = 1 - exp(-x / k[muscle][level]) on weekly effective sets; sets past 10 for one muscle in one session count at 50% (per-session cap). Next set = S(x+1) - S(x).
explain.why: Shows diminishing returns: the curve flattens, so the next set is worth more on an under-trained muscle. A model for comparing plans, not a measurement of growth.

items.formula: targets.json curve: S(x) = 1 - exp(-x / k[muscle][level]), x = weekly effective sets after session_discount | targets.json curve.marginal: S(x+1) - S(x) | targets.json curve.session_discount {cap: 10, factor: 0.5}; same threshold as rules junk_volume_session

items.label: Lower-back fatigue between days
items.description: Notes a heavy hinge the day before heavy squats, and (beginner level) heavy squats and deadlifts on the same day, naming the days and lifts.

explain.what: Notes a heavy hinge the day before heavy squats, and (beginner level) heavy squats and deadlifts on the same day, naming the days and lifts.
explain.how: Good: heavy hinges and heavy squats on non-adjacent days. Noted: heavy_hinges on day d and heavy_squats on day d+1, or both on one beginner day. Info severity in round 2 (was warn).
explain.why: The evidence is thin. The idea is that the lower back and hips need time between heavy hinges and squats, but in the one direct comparison we found, recovery after deadlifts was not slower than after squats or bench press (Belcher 2019). So this is shown as a note to consider, not a check, and it never blocks a program.

checks_pass.definition: pass = applicable kind=check items in pass; total = applicable kind=check items. Applicable: level in item.applies.levels and every item.applies.requires met (baseline_saved, training_days>=2). Info items never count.

Unfilled template slots are not tiles and are never checked.
analysis_metrics.rule_categories: Every rules[] entry has category (the section of its item) and metric (the id of the analysis item that shows it). The owning item decides whether a flag counts toward checks_pass.

progress.note: Progress stats from logged (completed) workouts only. A model for spotting trends, not a measurement of growth or strength. Every threshold here is modeled. Spec: data/progress-spec.md; reference: tools/progress.py.

reuses.e1rm: logger.e1rm_formula (epley) on working sets with reps <= logger.e1rm_max_reps (10); set_tags pr_exclude; deload sessions left out
reuses.lift_trend: logger.progress_signals (4-week window, >= 3 sessions over >= 14 days, up > +0.5 %/wk, dropping < -1.0 %/wk)

progress.weeks: Weeks start Monday (local). The in-progress week is never used for trends or refinements.

weekly_sets.plan: routine planned sets x rating (rating >= 0.25), summed over the routine days (no hard-set credit discount)

trend.rule: last 4 completed weeks, weeks with no completed session left out; >= 3 weeks needed. Least-squares slope of actual sets vs week index, as % of the mean: up > +5 %/wk, down < -5 %/wk, else flat; mean 0 -> flat.

main_lift.rule: Among exercises with a progress_signals trend in the window and rating[m] >= 0.5: type primary first, then accessory, then isolation; then the higher rating; then more sessions; then id. Reports first and last e1RM in the window, %/week and status.

adherence.rule: Sum completed_analytics adherence over the last 4 completed weeks: sets_ratio = completed planned sets / planned sets; sessions_ratio = completed / (completed + skipped). Per muscle: sum actual / sum plan over the weeks that had a completed session.

notes.rule: For exercises with rating[m] >= 0.5: Always notes = history.exNotes[exercise] (sticky), This session notes = entries[].notes of completed sessions. Always notes first (exercise id order), then This session notes newest first; at most 3 in total.

guards.rule: No refinement fires before 4 completed sessions spanning 2+ weeks. Each refinement has its own minimum below. One workout never triggers anything.

stall.rule: Per routine exercise: its last 4+ non-deload exposures (sessions with a valid e1RM) span >= 21 days, and the best e1RM of the last 3 is not above the best before them x (1 + review.flat_pct/100).
stall.rep_range_change: median top-set reps of the last 3 exposures vs the midpoint of rep_range(exercise, goal): midpoint = floor((low + high) / 2); at or below it -> suggest midpoint .. high, above it -> low .. midpoint. Display only; no board edit (the rep range is a target, not a tile field). Time-based ranges (holds) get no rep change.
stall.swap_variation: first tools/swap.py swaps(id, n=40) candidate that is eligible for the exercise's own template slot (tools/templates.py eligible(rule_for(id), level): same slot, type, movement_pattern and, for isolation, primary muscle; level filters) and not already in the routine, same equipment family first (swap.fam), -> {op: swap} on every routine tile of the exercise, same sets.

missed_sets.rule: Per routine exercise: of the last 3 completed sessions that planned it (session snapshot), at least 2 have fewer done working sets than planned (a skipped entry counts 0).
missed_sets.trim_sets: set the routine tile to max(2, round(mean done over those sessions)), only if lower than planned -> {op: sets}.
missed_sets.move_sets: move the trimmed sets (at least 2) to the routine day that lacks the exercise and was completed most often in the last 4 completed weeks (then fewest sets, then week order) -> {op: sets} + {op: add}; offered only when it adds no non-info flag (fix_validation).

under_delivered.rule: Muscle with plan >= 2 sets: actual < plan x (1 - 0.25) in each of the last 2 completed weeks, each with >= 1 completed session.
under_delivered.causes: missed_sets (a missed_sets refinement on an exercise rating the muscle >= 0.5), else skipped_sessions (a skipped session in those weeks that planned an exercise rating the muscle >= 0.5), else swaps_or_logging (info only).
under_delivered.actions: missed_sets -> link to that refinement; skipped_sessions -> link to one skipped_day refinement per weekday; else no edit.

skipped_day.rule: One per routine weekday that had a skipped session behind an under_delivered muscle (the muscles are listed together, not one card each).
skipped_day.action: reschedule: move every tile of that day to the nearest empty weekday (earlier first on a tie) whose result adds no non-info flag -> {op: remove} x n + {op: add} x n; none -> info only.
